correctness.rationale: For m >= M with b^M>4(U+1), the normalized digit remainder lies outside [0,1) unless index jump equals appended length, even with unbounded t. The ensuing exact periodic-residue inequality permits directed cycles only at corrections 0 or -1, and their cycles have exactly the circular-gap budget. All positive and negative correction cases, singleton/missing residue sets, and finite-walk bounds are proved algebraically. Replayed standalone verification performs 930021 exhaustive finite cyclic-placement comparisons and 825308 independent randomized checks; its finite range is supplementary.

value.rationale: The resonant integer-root family is a natural boundary case alongside known digit-walk termination theorems. The result gives an all-period, all-base exact minimum digit cap through the canonical largest circular gaps of two level sets, explicitly produces every existence class, and proves uniformly finite walks in the complementary cases. The exact classification is structural, not a fixed numerical exercise.
